deepdive.sec: Power / Grid Equipment & Energy Transition — diversified IPP (thermal + renewable + storage) with backward-integrated equipment manufacturing

bull_bear.body: The **INR 10,150 cr raise — the largest growth capital raise in the Indian power sector** — came in three parts: INR 3,000 cr promoter preferential (INR 1,125 cr received, INR 1,875 cr due before June 2027), INR 3,150 cr from selling 2.5 cr of 7 cr JSW Steel shares, and a INR 4,000 cr QIP. Result: INR 12,880 cr cash, leverage 4.95x from 5.2x, and enough to fund the equity portion of the INR 20,000 cr FY27 capex plus 2030 growth plans. FY27 funding maths given openly: ~INR 12,000-12,500 cr from raise plus operating cash; the balance to INR 20,000 cr is incremental debt (implying roughly INR 7,500 cr). Inorganic activity continues selectively (Maruti Clean Coal, GE boilers, TJPS stake-up, KSK 26% call option). Discipline signal: skipped the SECI pumped-hydro tender on a clearance technicality rather than stretching, and will only enter merchant BESS "when it makes sense that our benchmark returns are protected."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **PAT/ROE suppression persists** — the honest answer given was 4-5 years per asset for EBITDA-to-PAT translation. With ~3 GW/yr of additions, the drag is structural, not transitory.
- **TGNA curtailment**: 700 MW total (300 MW + 400 MW O2 Rajasthan) currently exposed; one conversion promised by 31-Aug, the other slipped to Sep/Oct.
- **Hydrology volatility** — a 26% portfolio generation decline on basin-level weakness (Sutlej −39%) with no company-specific mitigation beyond capacity charges.
- **Chinese equipment dependency** for the Mahanadi 4th unit, and **no long-term cell supply partnership** for BESS ("Right now, no") — warranties sit with the OEM cell maker.
- **Leverage stays high** at ~4.95x with a 2030 target of merely "below 5 times" — this is a levered compounder by design.
- Net debt of ~INR 55,000 cr against INR 3,103 cr of quarterly EBITDA; interest at INR 1,519 cr consumes roughly half of EBITDA.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Detailed and numerate, with a strong bias to giving checkable specifics — plant-level PLF explanations, the exact seasonal solar PLF curve, the funding bridge arithmetic, the BESS margin in $/kWh, the curtailment revenue impact in rupees. Where they declined (project-level pumped-hydro capex, FY28 guidance) they said so and committed to a date. The CEO was willing to accept an analyst's INR 5 cr/MW benchmark rather than dodge it ("Not very far from this number"). Notably, every softer PLF number was explained with a specific, verifiable cause (planned shutdown, force majeure, basin hydrology) rather than generic macro. The one area of visible reticence is Mahanadi units 5-6 and FY28, both deferred to "the right time very soon."
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The flat P&L is the intended output of the strategy, not a failure of it.** 1,558 MW of YoY additions produced zero revenue growth because generation fell on hydrology and planned outages, while depreciation and interest fully capitalised. Investors modelling EBITDA growth off capacity growth will keep being wrong for several more quarters.
- **Curtailment is nearly costless where GNA exists.** 69 MU of curtailment cost only ~INR 15 cr because GNA backdowns are deemed availability — the tariff is still earned. The real exposure is confined to the two TGNA projects.
- **JSW is now an equipment manufacturer that happens to own power plants.** With TJPS at 2x800 TG and GE Durgapur heading to 1.6 GW of boilers, it controls the scarcest input in Indian thermal — and management explicitly said this covers "both our current projects and future opportunities," i.e. potential third-party sales optionality.
- **Buyers are actively preferring 600 MW and smaller units** because deeper backdown at 50% is easier with high solar penetration — a demand-side quirk that makes Mahanadi's 600 MW unit easier to tie up than a 800 MW block.
- Pumped hydro's "significantly high-teen IRRs" against a mid-teen corporate benchmark is the highest-return asset class management named on the call, and 3,000 MW of it is already PPA-contracted.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- ₹10,150 Cr raised for growth and deleveraging: ₹4,000 Cr QIP (25th May), ₹3,150 Cr gross proceeds from partial JSW Steel stake sale (2.5 Cr of 7 Cr shares, 18th May) and ₹3,000 Cr preferential allotment to promoters (₹1,125 Cr received; balance before June 2027).
- Net debt ₹61,322 Cr at Jun-26 (TTM net leverage 5.53x), split operational net debt ₹54,885 Cr and CWIP net debt ₹6,437 Cr; ND/Equity fell to 1.70x from 2.15x at Mar-26.
- Operational net leverage (ND excl. CWIP / EBITDA, TTM) improved to 4.95x — the deck describes this as improving "from ~5.2x (TTM) in FY26" while the chart shows 5.23x at Mar-26.
- Cash & cash equivalents of ₹12,881 Cr, described as sufficient with "future internal accruals to fund equity portion of estimated Capex till FY30 (~₹1.1 trillion)".
- Cash Return on Adjusted Net Worth fell to 14% (TTM Jun-26) from 18% at Mar-26, which the deck attributes to the QIP raising net worth (adjusted net worth ₹31,336 Cr vs ₹23,781 Cr).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Thermal (5.7 GW):** generation −6% YoY to 8 BU. Open capacity now **under 4%**. API4 coal index rose from $90 to $113 (+25%) YoY but the domestic-coal shift kept the portfolio resilient. Mahanadi's 85% annual plant-availability entitlement means fixed-charge income is recognised now with cash collection over the following 2-3 quarters.
- **Hydro:** capacity up (Tidong + Kutehr) but generation −26% on a late snowmelt and long winter. July recovery is strong — Karcham, Baspa and Kutehr all running above 100% PLF; management expects design energy for the full year and continues to earn capacity charges regardless.
- **RE:** solar generation +29%, wind +3% on 1,168 MW of added capacity. Q1 solar PLF 21% — management gave the seasonal shape explicitly: **Q1 ~22%, Q2 lower, Q3 26%, Q4 28%, annualised ~25%.** July wind PLF already 5-6% above June.
- **Equipment manufacturing:** TJPS stake raised from 2.4% to **10.7%**; Halol blade plant commissioned; 5 GWh BESS plant trials complete and supplying.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Integration speed on acquisitions:** Tidong was acquired in January 2026 and commissioned by Q1 FY27 — four months ahead of its October 2026 schedule. Management framed this as "a testament to the integration capabilities our teams bring to every acquisition."
- **Equipment supply-chain control** — the TJPS + GE boiler combination removes the single biggest execution constraint on 800 MW-class thermal in India.
- **Merchant exposure under 4%** with fixed-cost recovery even during backdowns — "we continue to recover our fixed costs in these kinds of backdowns. We are not kind of impacted."
- **Mine-mouth thermal cost position:** the Mahanadi 4th unit will be built "significantly lower than the benchmark per MW cost of capacity addition" and sits next to the mine — attractive on merchant *or* PPA.
- **Technical-minimum resilience:** while the industry runs below technical minimum during the midday solar peak, Utkal never went below 58-60% PLF and the fleet ran >85% PLF / >90% availability in July; capability to run below 50% already demonstrated at Ratnagiri and Vijayanagar.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Deck frames the portfolio as a "Diversified Fuel Source and Offtaker, leading to De-risked Business Model": installed 14,535 MW split Thermal 5,658 MW, Wind 3,125 MW, Solar 2,275 MW, Hydro 1,781 MW, Hybrid 1,696 MW (39% thermal / 61% renewables).
- Offtaker mix on installed capacity is spread across Group Captive 20%, SECI 12%, RJ 9%, UP 8%, PTC 7%, C&I 5% and others, with only 4% "Open"; on the installed + under-construction 28.1 GW portfolio Group Captive is 15% (4.1 GW) and Open 4% (1.1 GW).
- Backward integration is presented as a moat: a commissioned wind blade plant at Halol, Gujarat and a 5 GWh battery container assembly plant at Pune, described as "Well-positioned to comply with potential domestic content requirements for BESS through in-house manufacturing capabilities".
- Company describes the ₹10,150 Cr raise as the "Largest Growth Capital Raise in Indian Power Sector".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Definitive agreement signed on 13th June for the acquisition of the 300 MW Maruti Thermal Plant (Maruti Clean Coal & Power) at a broad enterprise value of ₹1,410 Cr and estimated FY26 EBITDA of ₹279 Cr; it has an LT PPA with Rajasthan discoms for 195 MW (net), 5% offtake to Chhattisgarh State at variable cost and 64 MW merchant exposure.
- [JV stake] Stake in the Toshiba JSW Power Systems JV increased to 10.7% from 2.4%, which the deck says "fortifies thermal growth".
- [Reclassification] 225 MW solar and ~639 MW wind capacity were reclassified as hybrid projects following revisions to Vijayanagar Group Captive PPA modalities.
- [Commissioning] 150 MW Tidong hydro on the Tidong river, Sutlej basin, Himachal Pradesh achieved COD on 12th June, ahead of the Oct'26 guidance, capturing the hydro season and generating synergies with Karcham Wangtoo.
- [Demand backdrop] Deck cites CEA data: all-India power demand up 8.5% YoY to 483 BUs in Q1 FY27 and record peak demand of 271 GW in May 2026.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA grew only 2% on flat revenue because generation fell 5% (hydrology + planned shutdowns + one-off Mahanadi evacuation) even as capacity rose 1,558 MW. Coal cost pressure was real (API4 +25% YoY) but blunted by the domestic-coal shift. The structural margin issue is below EBITDA: depreciation +20% and interest +16% as new assets capitalise, with interest charged to P&L staying elevated in the initial years because the construction-period moratorium ends at COD. Management's stated normalisation path is **4-5 years per asset** before EBITDA translates properly into PBT/PAT — an explicitly industry-wide mechanic, not a JSW-specific problem. Merchant tailwind is genuine: DAM prices rose from ~INR 4.40/unit in Q1 FY26 to **INR 5.10/unit in Q1 FY27 (+16%)**, against an FY26 average of INR 3.86.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (prior):** guided FY27 3 GW addition (~35-40% wind, ~50/50 H1/H2 split) and ~INR 20,000 cr capex; first 600 MW of KSK thermal optionality by mid-FY27; Halol blade plant commissioning H1 FY27; FY28+ ~3-3.5 GW RE/yr; 2030 targets of 30 GW generation, 40 GWh storage, net debt/EBITDA ~5-5.5x.
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** *Delivered:* Halol blade plant commissioned 8-Jun-2026 (H1 FY27 as promised); 873 MW added in Q1 and ~1.1 GW by call date = 36% of the 3 GW target, running ahead of a 50/50 half-year split; Tidong commissioned 4 months early. *Reaffirmed:* 3 GW / INR 20,000 cr FY27 plan "firmly on track"; FY28 addition "in the same range". *Tightened:* the 2030 leverage target is now stated as **below 5.0x** (from 5-5.5x guided in Q4) and already achieved at 4.95x. *Slipped:* the 400 MW O2 Power Rajasthan connectivity moved from July-end to Sep/Oct. *New:* INR 10,150 cr capital raise completed; Maruti Clean Coal 300 MW definitive agreement; TJPS stake 2.4% → 10.7%; GE boiler acquisition to close in Q2 FY27 and be de-bottlenecked to 1.6 GW; first external BESS order ~INR 440 cr with ~INR 150 cr annual EBITDA potential; pumped-hydro IRRs guided at "significantly high-teen" with ~INR 5 cr/MW capex; Chitradurga blade plant by FY27; Mahanadi 4th unit FY28 with 25-30% lower per-MW capex than Salboni.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (a) did the 300 MW TGNA convert to GNA by 31-Aug, (b) did the GE Durgapur boiler acquisition close in the quarter as promised, (c) O2 Rajasthan connectivity in Sep/Oct, (d) capacity run-rate vs the 3 GW target after 1.1 GW, (e) FY28 guidance finally issued, (f) Mahanadi units 5-6 strategy announcement, (g) Narihalla PPA signed, (h) whether PAT/ROE begins to improve or the capitalisation drag deepens._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **FY27: 3 GW capacity addition and INR 20,000 cr capex — "firmly on track"**, with ~36% of the capacity guidance already achieved by the call date.
- **All 1.9 GW of remaining FY27 capacity is "100% secured from connectivity and which is all commissioned also"** — >530 MW of it is group-captive/off-grid on a dedicated line (fully insulated from grid curtailment), the rest a mix of STU/CTU with connectivity already in place.
- **FY28: capacity addition "in the same range" (~3 GW)**; formal FY28 guidance deferred — "very soon, we will come back for FY28 also."
- **Net leverage below 5.0x by 2030** — a committed target; already at 4.95x.
- **Salboni Phase 1 (2x800 MW):** supplier deliveries and commissioning "in line with the PPA timelines"; TG order placed with TJPS, civil order placed, site work in full swing, 100% land acquired, all key clearances received.
- **Mahanadi 4th unit (600 MW): commissioning in FY28**, on track, orders placed and material under dispatch (Chinese suppliers, with import permission received). Units 5 and 6 (taking 1.8 → 3.6 GW) — strategy announcement "at the right time very soon".
- **Mahanadi doubling capex to be "at least 25% to 30% lower" per MW than the Salboni greenfield benchmark.**
- **GE Durgapur boiler acquisition to complete "by end of this quarter" (Q2 FY27)** — nameplate 1.1 GW, taken to **1.6 GW (2x800) with de-bottlenecking and minor investment** already planned, to match TJPS Chennai's 2x800 TG capacity.
- **Chitradurga wind-blade facility: commissioning by FY27** (Halol already commissioned 8-Jun-2026, 450 blades/yr ≈ 600 MW of installations).
- **BESS: ~INR 150 cr of annual EBITDA from the 5 GWh plant** at full running, on ~$15 mn of annual revenue at $2.75-3.00/kWh assembly margin. First large external order of **~INR 440 cr** received.
- **Pumped hydro: "significantly high-teen IRRs"** (vs the mid-teen benchmark), with capex "not very far from" INR 5 cr/MW. Bhavali (1,500 MW, MSEDCL PPA) fully ready — EC received, land majority acquired, forest Stage-1 received, civil order to L&T, electromechanical to Voith. Kandhaura (1,680 MW, 1,500 MW PPA with UP) — **readiness to start execution by the last quarter of FY27.**
- **TGNA→GNA conversions:** 300 MW currently curtailed "almost certain… before 31st August"; the 400 MW O2 Power Rajasthan project connectivity slipped from July-end to **September or October**.
- **KSK Mahanadi:** call option notice already issued on the remaining 26% stake — minority outflow to shrink substantially on close.
- **Funding of FY27 capex:** ~INR 7,000 cr raised plus operating cash gives ~INR 12,000-12,500 cr; the balance to INR 20,000 cr is the incremental debt requirement. **INR 1,875 cr of promoter preferential capital still to come** (last date June 2027).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- **1.9 GW of FY27 RE capacity remaining to commission**, fully connectivity-secured.
- **Contracted pumped hydro: 3,000 MW of PPAs signed** (Bhavali 1,500 MW with MSEDCL; Kandhaura 1,500 MW of 1,680 MW with UP). **Narihalla, Karnataka** — letter received, local clearances at an advanced stage, PPA expected soon.
- A further **~9 GWh pumped-hydro site is now ready** for future tenders (JSW skipped the recent SECI tender solely because forest Stage-1 clearance was a pre-condition it could not meet at any other site).
- **BESS: first large external order ~INR 440 cr** (200 MW / 400 MWh equivalent), plus small third-party supplies already delivered.
- **Maruti Clean Coal & Power (300 MW, Chhattisgarh):** definitive agreement signed. 195 MW net long-term PPA with Rajasthan discoms, 14 years residual PPA life; 5% at variable cost to Chhattisgarh discom; ~64 MW merchant. Coal via long-term SECL FSA + SHAKTI linkage.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Vertical integration is now essentially complete for the thermal build-out** — "we are totally de-risked in terms of the supply chain of boiler, turbine, generators for all our 800 MW expansion plants." TJPS Chennai 2x800 TG + GE Durgapur boiler at 1.6 GW post-debottlenecking.
- **BESS backward integration:** in discussion with technology partners to make cells in India rather than import, and to scale the container from 5 MWh to 6/7/8 MWh for better cost efficiency. Government PLI for cells is being evaluated.
- **Merchant BESS:** not yet, but actively explored — the logic given is compelling (existing solar sites, existing connectivity reusable post-solar-hours, DC-side-only solar capex to charge the battery, and thermal evening-peak capacity still years away).
- **Maruti Clean Coal brownfield:** management confirmed the option to "double the capacity or even more in the same plant" next to the coal mine.
- Mahanadi units 5 and 6 (1.8 → 3.6 GW) — announcement pending.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Operationally a landmark quarter — 873 MW added in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April (36% of the 3 GW FY27 target already banked), Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early, and a INR 10,150 cr capital raise completed that leaves INR 12,880 cr of cash and net leverage down to 4.95x from 5.2x. Financially it looks flat: revenue INR 5,437 cr flat YoY, EBITDA +2%, PAT down — because depreciation (+20%) and interest (+16%) capitalise ahead of the earnings from newly commissioned RE assets, a mechanic management says takes 4-5 years to translate into PBT/PAT. The equity story is therefore entirely about execution against the 3 GW / INR 20,000 cr FY27 plan and the vertical-integration build-out, not about this quarter's P&L.
